correctness.rationale: PASS: For independent hyperplane-null antipodally symmetric boundary laws on a full-dimensional centrally symmetric body in R4, any four sampled position vectors are linearly independent a.s. and the single linear circuit has nonzero magnitudes w_i. Convex gauge triangle inequality gives 2w_i<=W, and equality would produce an affine degeneracy under some signed configuration, so it is strict; the same rules out pair half-sum ties. Conditional on unoriented lines, 32 independent equally likely sign vectors give barycentric signs and histogram (2,10,20-2D,2D) of V=0,1,2,3, where D counts heavy pairs. Heavy pairs are intersecting edges in K5, hence D<=4 (star or triangle). Independently enumerated all 32 sign configurations for five distinct rational witness vectors, giving D=0..4; the convex hull of ±v_i with unique dependence and 2max w<W has all points exposed, and Minkowski rounding plus small antipodal smooth-patch distributions yields hyperplane-null laws preserving the strict inequalities. The finite sign check supports but does not imply arbitrary-body assertions.
